html:
SMTO-LLM-0096 — This model's settings don't fit together

GUID: b07a1220-9f42-499b-8dd6-268eb34f722a
Slug: model-configuration-invalid
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: readiness

What happened

  • SMTO checked the saved settings for this model and found values that can't work, such as an answer size as large as the model's whole memory, or no model set up at all. Nothing was sent to the model.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing. If the Main card says Not configured, enter its Endpoint and Model and select Save Main. If the message names Helper, set up the Helper card or turn on Allow fallback to Main for that call type. SMTO can't start a task when the model it needs has never been set up.
  2. On the card for the model that failed (Main, Helper or Vision), expand Limits and recovery. Make sure Output allowance is smaller than Context ceiling and no timeout is blank or negative. If an answer may fill the model's whole memory, no room is left for your request, so SMTO refuses to send it.
  3. If you changed individual values in that card's model settings, set Profile to Provider Defaults, then select Save for that card, for example Save Main. This clears custom values that don't fit and lets the model service use its own defaults.
  4. Select Check saved model on the same card, then start a new task. The check confirms the saved settings now pass, and only new tasks pick up the corrected settings.

What success looks like

  • Check saved model completes without this error, and a new task gets an answer from the model.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep resending work in the task that failed; it keeps its old settings, so start a new task instead.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The model client or route failed validation before any inference: for example the output allowance or reservation leaves no room for input in the context window, a timing or override value is invalid, no Main model is configured, or a call type requires Helper with fallback to Main turned off.

What this means

  • The client rejected the combination of model settings before inference. Output reservations must leave space for input, timing limits must be within their supported ranges, and execution overrides must satisfy the parameter catalog. The controller remains available for correction.

Why this can happen

  • The client rejected the combination of model settings before inference. Output reservations must leave space for input, timing limits must be within their supported ranges, and execution overrides must satisfy the parameter catalog. The controller remains available for correction.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the context/output relationship and invalid parameter indicators in Model Configuration.

How to fix it

  • Read the message in Technical details for the failing check. In Settings › Setup › Model routing, configure Main if it is missing; configure Helper or enable Allow fallback to Main for a call type that requires Helper; keep Output allowance and the profile's output reservation below the effective context window, keep timeouts within valid ranges, and reset invalid overrides by choosing the Provider Defaults profile. Saved changes apply to new tasks; tasks already accepted keep their snapshot.
  • Open Model Configuration and correct the reported parameter combination. Ensure reserved output is smaller than the context ceiling, restore invalid overrides to Provider Defaults, and keep timing controls within their displayed ranges. New tasks use the corrected settings after saving.

Relevant SMTO settings

  • Open Model Configuration: model-configuration / llm_context_window_tokens. Applies to: new task.
  • Start a new task after changing this setting. Active and resumed tasks retain their captured values.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded condition before trying the affected request again. Inspect existing operation receipts before resuming saved work.

How to verify the fix

  • A new task initializes the client and receives a valid model response with the corrected settings.

What not to do

  • Do not replay completed work or weaken authentication and certificate checks to clear this diagnostic.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic describes the observed failure; it does not establish the outcome of earlier operations.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
